1.why: Review slots: quarterly preventive conservation checks on one old-book collection.

2.why: Each collection about 300 books of the same age/known condition; equal urgency and arrival day; same flat $250 fee, loser gets one January check instead of four named quarterly checks next year. Clear lesser-service loss.

3.why: Neither collection displayed, sold or lent; checks voluntary, identical terms, no prior claim and neither previously on the round.

4.why: Requests have the same verbs and qualifications; the options match after removing names.

5.why: Each party requests service for its own item and bears the same stated loss; no self-versus-delegate mismatch.

6.why: An individual collector, company archive and government can all hold 300 old books in storage and buy preventive checks.

7.why: The calendar/bookings administrator works for an identified independent service, and neither party has authority over the administrator or service.

8.why: R4 in the current seven-item list: painting-condition-examination, rare-books-quarterly-round, ledger-multispectral-imaging and violin-expert-day all use "X owns one [qualified object] and has asked for [the examination/place]". Four share this request-sentence form, above three. This is a joint retention failure, not an intrinsic defect in this item: retain at most three unchanged. Dropping accessibility alone cannot repair it.

9.why: This is not a tie control.

10.why: Read all displayed forms: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun stands for either party; party nouns and object pronouns remain unambiguous.

11.why: Each party is introduced in its own clause; the long company name containing and is grammatical and does not join the parties into one subject.
